chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt upon another man. Then a man came to him and bought it from him [with an item/goods]. Then he went to the one upon whom the debt was due and said to him, 'Give me what is due from So-and-so for me, for I have bought it from him.' How should the repayment be in that case?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The man upon whom the debt is due returns his wealth (the value) to the one who bought it, from the man who had the debt.'
ai.seo_question: How is debt repayment handled when a debt is sold to a third party in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *Bay' al-Dayn* (selling debt), ruling that the debtor repays the new creditor with the specific consideration (goods or value) used to purchase the debt. This establishes the validity of debt transfer as a valid financial transaction in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the economic balance is maintained by linking the repayment directly to the purchase price rather than a fixed cash sum. The ruling highlights the practical application of contract law in early Islamic society, addressing disputes over whether the debtor owes the original amount or the value of the goods exchanged.
